title: Protocol for monitoring and analyzing single nucleotide incorporation by S. cerevisiae RNA polymerases
protocol: Turn on the 25°C water bath.
Turn on the QF instrument.
Replace the 18 MΩ water in the quench drive syringe with 1 M HCl using 10 mL syringes.
Lower the drive platform to contact the drive syringes.
Exchange the residual 18 MΩ water in the quench line for 1 M HCl.
Set all valves to FIRE.
Input any reaction time into the QF keypad.
Move the 8-way valve to the reaction loop indicated upon input of reaction time.
Position an empty 1.5 mL collection tube at the end of the exit loop to collect expelled reaction solution.
Press GO on the keypad.
Collect four more identical reactions in the same 1.5 mL tube and discard.
Set drive valves to LOAD and EC/NTP valves to FLUSH.
Attach vacuum to EC and NTP flush lines.
Wash each reaction loop and sample loops with ≈ 500 μL 18 MΩ water.
Allow the system to dry for 30 seconds after each wash step.
Wash each reaction loop and sample loops with ≈ 500 μL MeOH.
Allow the system to dry for 30 seconds after each wash step.
Wash EC and NTP sample loops through their respective ports with 1 mL syringes loaded with ≈ 1 mL 18 MΩ water.
Allow the system to dry for 30 seconds after each wash step.
Wash EC and NTP sample loops through their respective ports with 1 mL syringes loaded with ≈ 1 mL MeOH.
Thaw DTT, BSA, RNA:DNAt, DNAnt, and heparin on ice.
Label 1.5 mL tubes required for one time course.
Aliquot 40 μL of bromophenol blue loading dye into each tube and store at -20°C until use.
Add 18 MΩ water to the EC mix tube and place it on ice.
Add 10 × buffer A, DTT, and BSA to the EC mix tube.
Add RNA:DNAt to the EC mix tube and mix by pipetting; return the RNA:DNAt to -20°C freezer immediately after use.
Add Pol fraction to the EC mix tube, mix by pipetting, and leave on ice for 10 min.
Return the Pol fraction to the −20°C freezer immediately.
Incubate the EC mix tube at ≈ 20°C for 20 minutes.
Add DNAnt and mix by pipetting.
Incubate at ≈ 20°C for 40 minutes.
Remove α-32P-CTP from the −20°C freezer to thaw at ≈ 20°C behind plexiglass shielding.
Prepare NTP mix and place on ice.
Prepare label mix and place on ice.
Add α-32P-CTP to the label mix once it is thawed.
Place the label mix on ice behind plexiglass shielding after adding α-32P-CTP.
Prepare chase mix and place on ice.
Label ECs with α-32P-CTP.
Incubate labeled ECs for 40 minutes with DNAnt.
Transfer 29.5 μL of label mix to the EC mix tube.
Mix by pipetting.
Incubate labeling reaction behind plexiglass shielding at ≈ 20°C for 10 minutes.
Place NTP mix at ≈ 20°C while labeling is ongoing.
Add 29.5 μL of chase mix to the EC mix after 10 minutes.
Mix by pipetting.
Collect time zero reactions by mixing radiolabeled EC mix with 1 × buffer A.
Input 0.005 s into QF keypad.
Move 8-way valve to designated loop based on QF calibration.
Load EC mix into QF using a P1000 pipette.
Remove vacuum before loading the EC mix into the QF.
Remove any bubbles from the syringe by gently tapping and moving the plunger back and forth.
Attach the syringe to the EC port, set EC valve to LOAD, and inject EC solution up to the ferrule going into the 8-way valve.
Set EC valve to FIRE.
Load 1 × buffer A opposite of the EC mix in the QF in the NTP port.
Transfer ≈ 200 μL of 1 × buffer A to a 1 mL syringe via a P1000 pipette.
Attach the syringe to the NTP port, set NTP valve to LOAD, and inject 1 × buffer A up to the ferrule going into the 8-way valve.
Set NTP valve to FIRE.
Set drive syringe valves to FIRE.
Position the time zero collection tube at the end of the exit loop to collect expelled reaction solution.
Press GO on the keypad.
Collect reaction solution and place the collection tube aside at ≈ 20°C.
Clean the reaction loop and sample loops by washing with ≈ 500 μL 18 MΩ water followed by ≈ 500 μL MeOH to dry.
Add equalizing 1 M HCl (varying volumes depending on calibration) to the collection tube containing the reaction solution.
Mix by pipetting.
Add 115 μL neutralization buffer to the collection tube.
Mix by pipetting.
Transfer 20 μL to its labeled dye tube containing pre-aliquoted 40 μL bromophenol blue loading dye.
Leave dye tube at ambient room temperature until the full time course is collected.
Collect the second time zero reaction.
Remove vacuum.
Set EC valve to LOAD and inject EC solution up to the ferrule going into the 8-way valve.
Set EC valve to FIRE.
Set NTP valve to LOAD and inject 1 × buffer A up to the ferrule going into the 8-way valve.
Set NTP valve to FIRE.
Repeat previous steps for days 21d through 21k.
Collect individual time points (0.005–10) s by mixing radiolabeled EC mix with NTP mix.
Clear 1 × buffer A from the QF.
Set NTP valve to LOAD and inject remaining 1 × buffer A solution into the sample loop.
Remove empty syringe.
Load ≈ 500 μL 18 MΩ water into a 1 mL syringe and inject it through the NTP port to clean the NTP sample loop.
Repeat with ≈ 500 μL of MeOH.
Randomly select the next time point.
Enter the selected reaction time into the keypad.
Move the 8-way valve to the designated reaction loop.
Load the NTP mix into the QF.
Remove vacuum from the system.
Transfer the NTP mix to a 1 mL syringe via a P1000 pipette.
Attach the syringe to the NTP port.
Set the NTP valve to LOAD and inject the NTP solution up to the ferrule going into the 8-way valve.
Set the NTP valve to FIRE.
Inject the EC mix up to the 8-way valve.
Set the EC valve to LOAD and inject the EC mix up to the ferrule going into the 8-way valve.
Set the EC valve to FIRE.
Collect the time point reaction solution.
Set the drive syringe valves to FIRE.
Position the collection tube at the end of the exit loop.
Press GO on the keypad to start collecting the reaction solution.
Place the collected reaction tube aside after collection is complete.
Clean the reaction loop as described for time zeros (step 21 h).
Add equalizing 1 M HCl to the collection tube containing the reaction solution.
Mix by pipetting.
Add 115 μL neutralization buffer to the collection tube.
Mix by pipetting.
Transfer 20 μL to its labeled dye tube.
Randomly select the next time point, enter the reaction time into the keypad, and move the 8-way valve to designated reaction loop.
Inject the NTP mix up to the ferrule going into the 8-way valve.
Set NTP valve to FIRE.
Repeat steps for the remaining time points.
Once the full time course is collected, store dye tubes at −20°C.
Clean QF.
Refill EC and NTP drive syringes with 18 MΩ water.
Wash EC and NTP sample loops through their respective ports with a 1 mL syringe loaded with ≈ 1 mL of 1 M NaOH.
Repeat wash with ≈ 1 mL of 18 MΩ water, then ≈ 1 mL of MeOH.
Wash quench drive syringe with 18 MΩ water and store in 18 MΩ water.
Exchange the residual HCl in the quench line for 18 MΩ water.
Wash each reaction loop with 1 M NaOH, 18 MΩ water, and MeOH.
Turn off 25°C water bath, vacuum, and QF instrument.
Pour 28% acrylamide gel.
Prepare running buffers.
Anode buffer is 1 × TBE.
Cathode buffer is 1 M NaOAc in 1 × TBE.
Set up gel rig with polymerized gel and running buffers.
Use a syringe with a needle tip to remove bubbles from the bottom of the plates submerged in cathode buffer.
Attach a heat dispersion plate to the back of the gel plates.
Attach temperature probe to the front of the gel plates.
Heat dye tubes at 95°C for 5 minutes.
Remove comb from the gel and use a syringe with a needle tip to remove residual urea from each well.
Load 15 μL bromophenol blue loading dye in wells 1 and 20.
Load 15 μL of each sample in wells 2–19.
Return samples to −20°C for storage.
Run gel at 50°C and 50 W until the dye front reaches the bottom of the heat dispersion plate.
Break down gel.
Turn off power.
Remove heat dispersion plate, temperature probe, and anode/cathode leads.
Use a Geiger counter to evaluate if either the anode or cathode buffer is radioactive.
If radioactive, extract the radioactive buffer with a syringe into a shielded container and rinse the gel rig with deionized water in the sink.
If not radioactive, rinse the gel rig with deionized water in the sink.
Remove gel plates from the gel rig.
Separate the gel plates to reveal the gel.
Transfer the gel to a piece of Whatman filter paper.
Wrap gel with plastic wrap, ensuring full coverage.
Clean gel area.
Use a Geiger counter to scan all gel equipment and bench area.
Rinse gel plates, spacers, and comb in deionized water and store.
Expose gel to phosphor screen.
Blank phosphor screen on a white light box for 10 min.
Place plastic wrapped gel in a phosphor cassette and place the freshly blanked phosphor screen on top.
Close the cassette and place on a flat surface for exposure.
Scan phosphor screen with the GE Typhoon or equivalent.
Save a *.gel file for further analysis.
